- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage account sessions`

List the sessions that start in a window

Shows each session id with its first and last event time, repo, event count, cost and account label, oldest first. Use an id as the boundary of `account assign`. Times are on your local clock; add `--utc` for UTC. The window is the last 7 days unless `--from` and `--to` say otherwise.

Example: `playbook usage account sessions --from 2026-10-30 --to 2026-11-04`

- `--from <FROM>`: Start of the window, like 2026-10-30 or 2026-10-30T08:00
- `--to <TO>`: End of the window (not included)
- `--db <FILE>`: Usage database file to use instead of the default, such as a backup copy
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage account undo`

Reverse the newest applied move, or the one with this number

- `<ID>`: Move number printed by `account assign`
- `--db <FILE>`: Usage database file to use instead of the default, such as a backup copy
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage collect`

Run the local OpenTelemetry receiver in the foreground

Listens on 127.0.0.1 only (default port 47318, chosen once and then kept; a free port is chosen on the first run when that one is taken; an existing install keeps the port it recorded) and stores API request cost and token rows, tool call timings and API errors from Claude Code's JSON telemetry. Prompts, tool content, paths, emails and user ids are never stored. A second start reports the running collector (`playbook usage status` shows it too). It stops by itself after the idle time, counted from the last real telemetry request, so a status check does not keep it alive. Use `--idle-seconds 0` to keep it running in a tmux window. Sessions that sent no telemetry are read from transcripts as before. While it runs, `cc` points its sessions at it unless `usage.telemetry` is `off` or you set telemetry yourself. When the settings that `setup` wrote point at it and none runs, playbook commands and hooks start one with `--idle-seconds 0` (see `docs/internals/04-usage-dashboard.md`).

Example: `playbook usage collect --idle-seconds 1800`

- `--port <PORT>`: Port to listen on. It is an error when the port is busy. Defaults to the recorded port, chosen once (47318, or a free one when that is taken) and kept. A port given here also replaces the recorded one; run `playbook setup --only telemetry` afterwards (older versions: `playbook init --only telemetry`)
- `--idle-seconds <IDLE_SECONDS>`: Stop after this many seconds with no request; 0 means never
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage doctor`

Show where pbtop can read your usage limits on this machine

Lists which sources exist: the plan fields and cached usage numbers in the Claude Code config file (`~/.claude.json`), the statusline reading and the manual `usage.budget.*` keys. It prints field names, ages, the plan label, the window percentages and the manual budget amounts, and never an email, name, id, organization or token. Run it on a machine where the limits look wrong and share the output. Add `--raw` to also print the values of six plan fields (billing type, organization type, seat tier, the two rate limit tiers and the extra usage flag) and the numbers behind each choice: the cache fetch time as written, the type of each cache field, and the monthly amount used against the reported limit and your budget, in dollars. It also says what the statusline budget line will show. It only reads files and creates nothing.

Example: `playbook usage doctor --raw`

- `--raw`: Also print the plan field values and the cached spend limit
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage machine`

Show this machine's id and name, or rename it

The id is a random UUID made once and kept in the data folder, so it survives a changed hostname or home folder. The name defaults to the hostname. Both stay on this machine.

Example: `playbook usage machine --name laptop`

- `--name <NAME>`: Display name to keep for this machine; an empty name restores the hostname
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage prune`

Delete old telemetry rows

Removes telemetry rows older than `usage.telemetryRetentionDays` (default 90, 0 keeps them) and the oldest rows beyond `usage.telemetryMaxRows` per table (default 500000, 0 means no limit). The receiver does the same when it starts and every few hours. Transcript data and every total are left alone, because totals come from transcripts.

Example: `playbook usage prune --dry-run`

- `--dry-run`: Say what would be removed without deleting anything
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage status`

Show whether the telemetry receiver is running

Prints how telemetry is configured (on with the collector running, off because you disabled it in your Claude Code settings, or off because nothing sets it) with a one-line fix, then the pid, port, idle limit, how many telemetry rows are stored (API requests, tool calls, API errors, metric points), the retention limits, and the time of the newest event. Like most playbook commands it can start the collector first. It never prints the token. With `--json` it prints the same as JSON. Exit code 0 whether or not a receiver runs.

Example: `playbook usage status --json`

- `--json`: Print the status as JSON
- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook usage stop`

Stop the running telemetry collector

Asks the collector that holds the lock to stop through its authenticated shutdown route and waits up to 3 seconds for it to let go. One that does not answer is killed, but only after checking that the process is really the playbook collector. Prints `stopped`, or `not running` with exit code 0 when no collector runs. The next playbook command or session starts a new one. A collector from 0.38.0 or older holds no lock, so this does not see it.

Example: `playbook usage stop`

- `--utc`: Show times and group days in UTC. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`
- `--local`: Show times and group days in your local time zone. This is the default. Overrides `usage.timeZone` and `PLAYBOOK_TELEMETRY_TZ`

### `playbook version`

Print the installed version, same as `--version`

### `playbook watch`

Poll GitHub issues and comments and act on them by rules

Rules live in `watch.rule.<id>` and `watch.repos` lists the repos. At the default level a matching event becomes a proposal that nothing acts on until you approve it. The GitHub token is read from the environment variable named by `watch.tokenEnv` (`GITHUB_TOKEN` when unset).

With no verb it runs in the foreground until you stop it, polling every `watch.pollSeconds` and picking up after a laptop sleep from where it stopped. A second foreground run prints `watch already running` and exits 1.

Example: `playbook watch once`

Subcommands: `approve`, `dry-run`, `install-service`, `log`, `once`, `pause`, `reject`, `resume`, `retry`, `status`, `uninstall-service`

### `playbook watch approve`

Carry out a proposal

Runs the action now. When another watch process is running it only marks the item and that process carries it out.

Example: `playbook watch approve 3`

- `<ID>`: Proposal number printed by `watch once`

### `playbook watch dry-run`

Show the rules and what a poll would propose, and change nothing

Example: `playbook watch dry-run`

- `--since <SINCE>`: Look at events from this UTC time, for example 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z

### `playbook watch install-service`

Install a timer that runs `watch once` every 60 seconds

A launchd agent on macOS and a systemd user timer on Linux. No process stays running between polls. The timer finds the GitHub token through `gh auth token`, so run `gh auth login` first.

Example: `playbook watch install-service`

### `playbook watch log`

Print the audit log, oldest first

Example: `playbook watch log --rule triage --outcome done`

- `--rule <RULE>`: Only records of this rule
- `--outcome <OUTCOME>`: Only records with this outcome, such as `done` or `retry`
- `--json`: Print each record as a JSON line

### `playbook watch once`

Poll every repo once and run the items you approved

A repo watched for the first time starts from now, so turning watch mode on never replays old issues. Prints `watch already running` and exits when another watch process holds the lock.

Example: `playbook watch once --since 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`

- `--since <SINCE>`: Replay events from this UTC time, for example 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z

### `playbook watch pause`

Stop starting new actions

An action that is already running finishes. Proposals still queue.

Example: `playbook watch pause`

### `playbook watch reject`

Drop a proposal without acting on it

Example: `playbook watch reject 3`

- `<ID>`: Proposal number printed by `watch once`

### `playbook watch resume`

Start new actions again after a pause

Example: `playbook watch resume`

### `playbook watch retry`

Put a dead item back in the queue

Example: `playbook watch retry 3`

- `<ID>`: Number of the dead item, shown by `watch status`

### `playbook watch status`

Show whether watch runs, the queue, the limits and the dead list

Example: `playbook watch status --json`

- `--json`: Print the status as JSON

### `playbook watch uninstall-service`

Remove the timer that `install-service` made

The audit log stays unless you ask for it to go.

Example: `playbook watch uninstall-service --delete-log`

- `--delete-log`: Also delete the audit log

### `playbook worktree`

Clean up git worktrees whose branches have landed

Locked worktrees are kept unless the process that locked them is gone.

Example: `playbook worktree sweep --dry-run`

Subcommands: `remove`, `review`, `sweep`

### `playbook worktree remove`

Remove one worktree if it has landed and is not in use

Example: `playbook worktree remove ../.worktrees/my-repo/my-branch`

- `<PATH>`: Worktree path, as shown by `git worktree list`

### `playbook worktree review`

Create or remove the locked review worktrees

`/playbook:review --quick` and `/playbook:review --deep` run in them.

Subcommands: `setup`, `teardown`

### `playbook worktree review setup`

Add a locked worktree for a PR head and print its path

Fetches the PR head, adds a locked detached worktree for it, and prints its absolute path on stdout. Warnings go to stderr.

Example: `playbook worktree review setup 12 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`

- `<PR>`: PR number
- `<HEAD_SHA>`: Full head commit sha the review was resolved against

### `playbook worktree review teardown`

Remove a review worktree, even a dirty one

Always exits 0, and skips any path outside the review worktrees.

Example: `playbook worktree review teardown .git/review-worktrees/12-0123456`

- `<PATH>`: Worktree path printed by `setup`

### `playbook worktree sweep`

Remove every landed worktree that is not in use

Scans all worktrees of this repo, whichever tool made them. Keeps locked ones unless the locking process is dead.

- `--dry-run`: Show what would be removed without removing anything
